names: why area of circle is pi r square
subject: maths

asks: A labelled diagram of a circle cut into sixteen equal slices, and beside it the same slices laid in a row, alternately pointing up and down, showing the radius and the long side.
A drawing of a paper circle folded into eight equal sectors, and beside it the cut sectors arranged alternately up and down into a shape like a rectangle.
picture.why: Slices laid alternately up and down turn a round shape into an almost-rectangle whose sides are the radius and half the circumference.

big_idea.text: The area of a circle is π × r × r, because it can be rearranged into a rectangle that is half the circumference long and one radius tall.

objectives.can: Work out the area of a circle from its radius
Explain why the area is half the circumference times the radius
Predict how the area changes when the radius is doubled

why_it_matters.text: It tells you how much space a round thing covers, a chapati, a round field or a well's lid, from one length you can measure.

the_why.text: Cut a circle into many thin slices and lay them alternately up and down: they make a shape very close to a rectangle whose height is the radius and whose length is half the round edge, π × r, so its area is π × r × r.

picture.text: A circle of radius 7 cm cut into 16 equal slices in two colours. The slices slide into a row, alternately pointing up and down: the shape is nearly a rectangle with wavy top and bottom. Its height is marked as the radius and its length as half the circumference. With more, thinner slices the waves flatten.
picture.standard: circle cut into sectors and rearranged into a rectangle

card.diagram_ask: A labelled diagram of a circle cut into sixteen equal slices, and beside it the same slices laid in a row, alternately pointing up and down, showing the radius and the long side.

needs_first.text: The circumference of a circle is 2 × π × r.
The area of a rectangle is length times breadth.

mistakes.mistake: Using the diameter in place of the radius: π × 14 × 14 for a circle of radius 7.
mistakes.why_it_fails: The height of the rearranged rectangle is the radius, not the diameter, so using the diameter gives four times the area.

mistakes.mistake: Giving the circumference, 2 × π × r, as the area.
mistakes.why_it_fails: The circumference is a length around the edge; the area is the space inside, which needs the radius twice.

mistakes.mistake: Thinking that doubling the radius doubles the area.
mistakes.why_it_fails: Doubling the radius makes the rectangle twice as long and twice as tall, so the area becomes four times as much.

opening_question.question: A round chapati has a radius of 7 cm. How many 1 cm squares would it take to cover it?

route.what: Show the circle of radius 7 cm and ask how many 1 cm squares cover it. Ask for a guess.
Square tiles do not fit a round edge. Cut the circle into 16 equal slices instead.
Lay the slices in a row, alternately up and down. Ask: what shape does this look like? Nearly a rectangle.
Mark the sides: the height is a radius, and the length is half the round edge, half of 2 × π × r, which is π × r. Cut thinner slices: the waves flatten.
Area = length × height = π × r × r, written πr².
Radius 7 cm: half the circumference is 22 cm, and 22 × 7 = 154 square cm.
Using the diameter 14 gives 616, four times too much, because the rectangle's height is the radius.
Radius 14 cm: the learner finds 616 square cm, four times 154, before it is shown.
The learner says where π × r and r come from in the rectangle.

questions.question: A circle has radius 7 cm. What is its area? (take π = 22/7)
questions.explain: Half the circumference is 22 cm and the height is 7 cm, so 22 × 7 = 154; 44 is the circumference and 616 uses the diameter.

questions.question: A circle's radius is doubled from 7 cm to 14 cm. What happens to its area?
options: It becomes four times as much
It grows by 44 square cm, one more circumference
questions.explain: The rectangle becomes twice as long and twice as tall, so its area is 2 × 2 = 4 times as much.

try_it.title: Circle into rectangle
materials: a round lid or steel plate to trace
try_it.stands_for: The paper circle is the circle; each folded slice is a sector; the ruler measures the rectangle's sides.
try_it.predict: When you lay the slices alternately up and down, will the height of the shape be the radius or the diameter?
steps: Trace a round lid on paper and cut out the circle.
Fold it in half three times and open it to see eight equal slices.
Lay the slices in a row, alternately pointing up and down.
Measure the height of the shape and the radius of the circle with the ruler.
try_it.observe: The slices make a shape close to a rectangle with wavy edges; its height is the same as the radius, and its length is about half the way round the circle.
try_it.question: Why is the area of this rectangle the same as the area of the circle?
try_it.expected: Because it is made of exactly the same pieces moved around, and its height is the radius and its length is half the circumference, π × r, so the area is π × r × r.
try_it.write: A circle cut into slices makes a rectangle π × r long and r tall. So the area of a circle is π × r × r.
try_it.in_class: Pairs, each tracing a lid. The teacher draws the rearranged slices on the board and labels one side r and the other side ?. Ask: what is the long side, and why? A pair that says 2πr has not seen that half the slices point up and half point down.
